youtube.title: How Rust Is Memory Safe Without a GC 🦀

sub: So how does Rust do it?
scenes.say: No garbage collector, and no dangling pointers. So how does Rust do it?

scenes.heading: Every value has one owner
scenes.say: Every value has exactly one owner. When you write let s2 equals s1, the String moves to s2, and s1 can't be used anymore.

scenes.heading: Use it after a move?
scenes.label: compile error, not a crash
scenes.say: Try to use s1 after the move, and the borrow checker stops you at compile time, before your program ever runs.

scenes.heading: Owner goes out of scope
scenes.say: And when the owner goes out of scope, Rust frees the memory automatically. No GC, no manual free.

scenes.heading: Learn more
question: Borrowing next?
